title: Direct flights to Christmas markets from UK airports (2026)
author: Brogan
intro: This winter there are more direct flights to Christmas markets from UK airports than ever, including easyJet's first flights to Nuremberg and new Strasbourg routes from Bristol and Luton. Here's which markets you can fly to from where, and how to time the trip.
seo_title: Direct flights to Christmas markets from the UK (2026)
seo_description: New for 2026: easyJet to Nuremberg and Strasbourg, Jet2 to Cologne from Bristol and more market flights from regional airports. Routes checked Nov 2026.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **New for 2026:** Nuremberg and Strasbourg
- **Most choice:** Jet2 and easyJet
- **Short season:** late Nov to Christmas
- **Best days:** midweek trips

We checked these routes in November 2026. Christmas market flights are seasonal and some only run a few weeks, so check the airline's timetable for your dates before booking a hotel.

Jet2 also added Strasbourg to its Christmas markets programme this winter, which works for [Colmar](/destinations/colmar) too, about half an hour away by train.

sections.heading: The classic markets from regional airports
sections.text:
Jet2 runs a big Christmas markets programme from its UK bases, with flights and city-break packages to the best-known markets. For 2026/27:

- **East Midlands:** Berlin, Budapest, Gdańsk, Kraków, Prague and Vienna.
- **Birmingham:** eight market cities, including Cologne and the new Copenhagen route.
- **Stansted:** extra flights to [Kraków](/destinations/krakow), [Prague](/destinations/prague) and [Vienna](/destinations/vienna).

Most of these only run from late November to the days before Christmas. If you want flights outside that window, the year-round easyJet, Ryanair and British Airways routes to cities like Prague and Vienna are the ones to look at.

sections.heading: Which market should you pick?
sections.text:
- **For the most traditional market:** [Nuremberg](/destinations/nuremberg), for the Christkindlesmarkt and gingerbread.
- **For a fairy-tale setting:** [Strasbourg](/destinations/strasbourg) or Colmar. Our guide to [Strasbourg or Colmar at Christmas](/blog/strasbourg-or-colmar-at-christmas) compares them.
- **For lots of markets in one city:** [Cologne](/destinations/cologne), with several big markets within walking distance. See our [Cologne Christmas markets](/blog/cologne-christmas-markets-2026) guide.
- **For good value:** [Kraków](/destinations/krakow) or [Budapest](/destinations/budapest), where food and drink cost less than in Germany.

For a fuller comparison, read our [best Christmas markets in Europe](/blog/best-christmas-markets-in-europe) guide.

sections.heading: How to time the trip
sections.text:
Most markets open in the second half of November and close on or just before Christmas Eve, though some carry on into early January. The first two weeks of December are the busiest, especially at weekends.

On routes that only fly twice a week, the flight days decide your trip. A Monday and Friday route works for a long weekend (Friday to Monday) or a midweek break (Monday to Friday). Once you know the days, book the hotel to match, because market-town hotels fill up early.

Tip: go midweek if you can. Prices are lower, and the markets are far more pleasant without the Saturday crowds.

sections.heading: What to pack
sections.text:
- **Warm layers:** German and Central European markets are often around freezing in the evenings, and you'll be standing outside.
- **Waterproof shoes:** cobbles and wet squares get slippery.
- **Cash and card:** most stalls take cards now, but a few small ones still prefer cash.
- **Hand luggage space:** for gifts, and remember the liquids rules if you're bringing back mulled wine or schnapps.

sections.heading: Package or flight only?
sections.text:
Jet2CityBreaks and other operators sell flights and hotels together for Christmas markets, which protects you if a flight is cancelled and often includes transfers. Booking flights and hotel separately can be cheaper and gives more choice of hotel, especially in smaller places like Colmar.

Watch out: some of the new routes fly to smaller airports outside the city. Check how far the airport is from the market and how you'll get there before you book, especially for a late-evening arrival.

If you'd rather not fly, our guide to [Christmas markets by train from London](/blog/christmas-markets-by-train-from-london) covers Bruges, Cologne, Paris and more. If your family can't agree which market, add a few to somewhere.party and let the draw decide.

faqs.question: Can you fly direct to Nuremberg from the UK?
faqs.answer: Yes. For winter 2026/27, easyJet flies to Nuremberg for the first time, from Gatwick, Luton and Manchester.

faqs.question: Can you fly direct to Strasbourg from the UK?
faqs.answer: Yes. easyJet flies from Bristol from 20 November 2026 and from Luton from 29 November 2026, and Jet2 has added Strasbourg to its Christmas markets programme.

faqs.question: Which UK airports have Jet2 Christmas market flights?
faqs.answer: Several of Jet2's bases do, including Birmingham, Bristol, East Midlands, Leeds Bradford and Stansted. Check Jet2's site for the destinations from your airport.

faqs.question: When are the Christmas markets open?
faqs.answer: Most open in the second half of November and close around Christmas Eve, though some run into early January. Check the dates for the market you're visiting.
